pitch.title: The Secret History of Control Y
pitch.hook: In nineteen sixty-eight, Warren Teitelman wrote a tiny line of code to fix his own mistyped commands.
pitch.angle: Most people assume keyboard shortcuts for undo and redo were designed as master features from the start. They were actually born out of sheer panic when early programmers kept wiping full pages of work with single keystrokes.
key_facts: Warren Teitelman created the first programming undo feature in nineteen sixty-eight.
Larry Tesler added the undo command to the Gypsy text editor at Xerox PARC in nineteen seventy-four.
Apple standard1zed Command Z for undo and Command Y or Shift Z for redo on the Lisa and Macintosh in the early nineteen eighties.
Early computing systems had no undo memory buffer, meaning one mistake destroyed hours of typing.
pitch.visual_style: retro ninety-style mechanical keyboard macro photography with glowing neon accent light

fact_check.claim: Warren Teitelman created the first programming undo feature in 1968.
Larry Tesler added the undo command to the Gypsy text editor at Xerox PARC in 1974.
Apple standardized Command Z for undo and Command Y or Shift Z for redo on the Lisa and Macintosh in the early 1980s.
Early computing systems had no undo memory buffer.
